text:
Boston's 5-1 win looks like a rout, and the numbers say it was one. BOS generated 3.13 expected goals to PHI's 1.34 and put up 64 shot attempts to 37. In a simulated replay of every shot, BOS wins 81 percent of the time. Pavel Zacha opened the scoring at 12:21 of the first on a 5 percent chance, the least likely goal of the night, and it set the tone for a game PHI chased from the start.

The pressure built steadily. Mason Lohrei made it 2-0 late in the second, and the third period belonged to the home side, which out-chanced PHI 1.37 to 0.46 in expected goals. Marat Khusnutdinov scored 1:55 in. Porter Martone cut it to 3-1 on a power play at 6:32, PHI's only goal, and it came on a chance worth just 8 percent. Casey Mittelstadt restored the three-goal margin at 9:21, and Fraser Minten finished the scoring at 15:59. Fraser Minten, the first star, had a goal and two assists. JJ Peterka (two assists) and Khusnutdinov took the other two stars.

The goaltending gap was real but not the whole story. Dan Vladar allowed 5 goals on 32 shots, about 1.9 more than the chances deserved, while Jeremy Swayman faced only 15 shots and stopped 14 of them. Even so, BOS controlled play at even strength, 3.11 expected goals to 1.22, so the result would have been lopsided regardless. PHI also gave the puck away 22 times to BOS's 13, a steady leak that fed the territorial edge.
